findings.evidence: Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Basic.lean:54 `... ↔ ∫⁻ a, (‖f a‖ₑ) ^ p.toReal ∂μ < ∞`; Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Real.lean:40 `@[simp] lemma enorm_eq_self (x : ℝ≥0∞) : ‖x‖ₑ = x := rfl`; Mathlib itself uses `rw [enorm_eq_self]` (LpSeminorm/Basic.lean:547) rather than defeq.
findings.fix: Make the collapse explicit with the existing simp lemma: at line 588 `have hMint : ... := by simpa only [enorm_eq_self] using (eLpNorm_lt_top_iff_... ).mp ...`, and at line 605 `simp [Real.enorm_toReal hx.ne]` (or `rw [enorm_eq_self]; exact Real.enorm_toReal hx.ne`).
findings.issue: `hMint` is ascribed `∫⁻ x, maximalFunction μ f x ^ p.toReal ∂μ < ∞`, but `eLpNorm_lt_top_iff_lintegral_rpow_enorm_lt_top` produces `∫⁻ a, ‖maximalFunction μ f a‖ₑ ^ p.toReal ∂μ < ∞`; the two match only by the undocumented defeq `‖a‖ₑ = a` for `a : ℝ≥0∞`. Same reliance at line 605, where `exact Real.enorm_toReal hx.ne` closes a goal whose RHS is `‖maximalFunction μ f x‖ₑ` rather than `maximalFunction μ f x`.

findings.evidence: Lines 583–614 only invoke `measurable_maximalFunction μ f` and `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_lt_top`. Mathlib has the L¹ analogue `integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top` (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/L1Space/Integrable.lean:925) but no Lᵖ counterpart (`grep memLp_toReal` in ./mathlib: no matches), so the general form is genuinely reusable.
findings.fix: State the general ℝ≥0∞-valued lemma once (measurability + `eLpNorm g p μ < ∞` ⇒ a.e. finiteness, seminorm equality, `MemLp` of the `toReal` representative) and derive the three maximal-function lemmas from it by supplying `measurable_maximalFunction` and `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_lt_top`.
findings.issue: `ae_maximalFunction_lt_top_of_memLp`, `eLpNorm_maximalFunction_toReal_eq` and `memLp_maximalFunction_toReal` use no property of `maximalFunction` beyond `Measurable` and `eLpNorm _ p μ < ∞`; the reusable fact (for `g : E → ℝ≥0∞` measurable with finite `eLpNorm` and `0 < p < ∞`: `g` is a.e. finite, `eLpNorm (fun x => (g x).toReal) p μ = eLpNorm g p μ`, hence `MemLp (toReal ∘ g) p μ`) is hidden inside maximal-function-specific statements.

summary: Two proofs silently pass through the definitional identity `‖a‖ₑ = a` on `ℝ≥0∞` instead of rewriting with `enorm_eq_self`, and the toReal/MemLp descent is stated only for `maximalFunction` although its proof uses nothing but measurability plus finite `eLpNorm`.
